transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-12-06
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Patel (Redwood SE), Daniel Reyes (CFO - Lighthouse), Priya Kapoor (VP Eng), Samir Das (Head MLOps)

Summary: Quick renewal + expansion check. Customer leaning toward dedicated capacity for predictability, wants EU region and SOC2/KMS details. Agreed to run benchmarks and share pricing.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. quick agenda: renewal timing, capacity needs, regions and security docs.
[00:18] Daniel: Yeah thanks Maya. we're pretty happy overall; main questions are cost predictability and EU residency for some of our clients. renewal's coming up end of month.
[00:30] Ethan: Hi all, i'm Ethan on infra, i'll be running the perf side. curious about current token volumes and peak concurrency so we can size dedicated pools.
[00:45] Priya: current production is about 60 qps avg, peaks around 220 qps during settlement windows, typical sequence lengths 128-512, embeddings workload separate.
[01:05] Samir: also we use an internal KV cache layer but it's small, keys per request vary, want to know how redwood's prefix caching and batching will interact.
[01:25] Maya: great — for renewal, we can extend hosted for another year, or move to dedicated which gives reserved GPU pools, lower p99 latency, and isolation. costwise dedicated is commit-based so we can show savings at scale.
[01:45] Daniel: what about burst windows? our end of quarter spikes are unpredictable.
[01:55] Ethan: dedicated supports burst capacity and we can configure autoscale policies; burst is priced differently but you can set thresholds and fallback to hosted if needed. we'll include an example in the pricing doc.
[02:20] Priya: EU region — we have GDPR clients and need data residency for a subset of tokens. can you run inference in eu-west?
[02:32] Maya: yes, we can add eu-west-1 as part of the dedicated contract or as an additional region on hosted. data plane can be pinned to EU and control plane kept in us if you want. we'll share details.
[02:50] Daniel: for SOC2 and KMS — we need encryption at rest and audit logs for tokens used in production, plus SSO for our ops team.
[03:03] Ethan: we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and detailed audit logs; SSO via SAML is standard. i'll attach the specific sections from our security pack.
[03:18] Priya: any worries about model fallbacks or quality if you route across regions? we can't have inconsistent behavior.
[03:30] Ethan: good question — we recommend pinning models per region or using a model-compatibility policy; redwood's routing can fallback to compatible quantized variants but we log regressions. we'll show a canary rollout example.
[03:50] Daniel: timeline — we want renewal signed by 12/31, ideally have benchmarks and pricing by mid-december.
[03:58] Maya: that's doable. i'll send updated pricing today/tomorrow for dedicated plus a 3-region option; ethan will set up the perf run on eu-west and us-west to capture p50/p95/p99 across routes.
[04:18] Samir: on benchmarks, we need 24 hour runs to hit the settlement patterns; can you simulate peak qps?
[04:25] Ethan: yes we can. please share sample request distributions and we will mirror seq lengths and KV cache hit rates.
[04:40] Priya: regarding contract extension — any flexibility on term lengths? we prefer 12 months but open to 24 if pricing helps.
[04:50] Maya: we can offer standard 12 or discounted 24 month commit; i'll include both in the quote with committed throughput tiers.
[05:05] Daniel: legal — our procurement needs a copy of SOC2 and some custom SLA language about P99 latency. is that possible?
[05:15] Maya: yes, i'll include the security pack and a draft SLA. for P99 we can include target latency and credits for breaches — subject to the Dedicated plan level.
[05:30] Samir: for KMS: do you support bring-your-own-key?
[05:35] Ethan: yes BYOK supported, we can integrate with AWS KMS or external HSMs, we have docs and runbooks.
[05:45] Daniel: competitors — we've chatted with openai and anthropic, bedrock; cost delta is the main differentiator plus region options.
[05:58] Maya: understood — our focus is predictable economics and observability. we'll highlight cost per 1M tokens and p99 latency targets in the quote.
[06:10] Priya: okay next steps: send pricing, schedule benchmark, share security docs.
[06:18] Maya: yep. i'll follow up with pricing and contractual options; ethan will reach out for perf details.
[06:25] Daniel: sounds good. one more ask: can we get a short exec-level summary for procurement?
[06:30] Maya: sure — i'll include a 1-page summary with key numbers and recommended plan.
[06:35] Priya: thanks everyone.
[06:38] Maya: thanks all — we'll follow up. call ends.
